title: [VSC-5] JetBrains: shared landing-policy corpus for the settings dialog
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). First wave: no dependencies, files disjoint from the other first-wave rows. JetBrains first: this row writes the held-out corpus that VS Code's settings row (VSC-10) must pass unchanged.

Reuse decision (VSC-0): one client-neutral JSON corpus per shared presentation, executed by both test suites (CQ-I06b pattern, moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json; rule in the header of ClientVerdictCorpusTest.kt). Each new corpus gets its own file.

Objective: JetBrains' settings dialog shows the effective landing policy read-only. MoeSettingsDialog.effectivePolicyRows(settings: ProjectSettings?) (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MoeSettingsDialog.kt, companion object) returns ordered PolicyRow(label, value, detail) rows in plain English: Auto-commit, Checkpoint commits, Push checkpoints, Commit board state, Commit hooks, Landing branch, Quality gate, Quality gate scope, Undeclared-file attribution, Plan size limits. VS Code has no such section. Pin the rows, including the defaults applied to missing fields, as a corpus.

Deliverable:
- new moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-settings-policy.json: `{ "version": 1, "rows": [ { "id": "P01", "settings": <project.settings wire JSON (partial) or null>, "expect": [ { "label", "value", "detail" } ] } ] }`. At least 10 rows: null settings (all defaults); `{}`; each boolean flipped; consolidationBranch empty, literal and glob; qualityGate empty and set; qualityGateScope everyTask and any other value; attribution.undeclared never, always, solo and an unknown value; custom taskSizing.
- new moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/SettingsPolicyCorpusTest.kt: parses `settings` through the same MoeJson path the client uses for STATE_SNAPSHOT project.settings (null stays null), asserts effectivePolicyRows equals `expect` exactly and in order, asserts unique `P[0-9]{2}` ids, and reports every failing id at once.
If a row exposes a JetBrains bug (for example a default that differs from the daemon's in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/persistence.ts), fix it here and name it in the summary.

Not in scope: VS Code files (VSC-10), MoeSettingsDialogTest.kt (unchanged), the daemon.

Verification (WSL has no JDK): take the `jetbrains-gradle` lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease); `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /mnt/d/moe-scratch/<dir>`; overlay this task's files; run `cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\moe-scratch\<dir>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun'` (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-snapshot-gradle-test); release the lease even on failure.
definitionOfDone: moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-settings-policy.json exists with version 1 and at least 10 rows with unique P[0-9]{2} ids, covering every case listed in the description.

SettingsPolicyCorpusTest.kt parses each row's settings through MoeJson and asserts effectivePolicyRows equals the row's expect list exactly (label, value, detail and order), reporting all failing ids at once.
A scratch-copy mutant that swaps the Commit board state On/Off value makes SettingsPolicyCorpusTest fail (mutant discarded afterwards).
The full JetBrains suite passes in a git-archive snapshot under the jetbrains-gradle lease: `gradlew.bat test --rerun` reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL, with the JUnit total in the summary.
The diff touches only the two new files, plus MoeSettingsDialog.kt or MoeJson.kt if a row exposed a JetBrains bug (named in the summary).

implementationPlan.description:
Write the held-out corpus moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-settings-policy.json with the Write tool.

Format: {"version": 1, "rows": [...]}. Each row is {id, note, settings, expect}:
- id: P01 to P19;
- note: a one-line reason;
- settings: the project.settings WIRE JSON, either null or an object that uses only the policy keys: autoCommit, checkpointCommits, checkpointPush, commitBoardState, commitHooks, consolidationBranch, qualityGate, qualityGateScope, attribution {undeclared}, taskSizing {warnSteps, maxSteps, warnDistinctFiles, maxDistinctFiles};
- expect: the full 10-entry list of {label, value, detail} in display order: Auto-commit, Checkpoint commits, Push checkpoints, Commit board state, Commit hooks, Landing branch, Quality gate, Quality gate scope, Undeclared-file attribution, Plan size limits. Copy the strings exactly from effectivePolicyRows, landingBranchRow and attributionRow in MoeSettingsDialog.kt.

Rows:
- P01: settings null (no snapshot yet), all defaults.
- P02: {}, all defaults; same expect as P01.
- P03: every landing boolean flipped: autoCommit, checkpointCommits, checkpointPush and commitBoardState false; commitHooks true.
- P04: consolidationBranch ''.
- P05: consolidationBranch '  release/train  ' (trimmed literal, the peel target).
- P06: consolidationBranch 'moe/work-*' (glob).
- P07: qualityGate ''.
- P08: qualityGate '  npm test  ' (trimmed, set).
- P09: qualityGateScope 'everyTask'.
- P10: qualityGateScope 'whenever' (unknown, so epic-final).
- P11 to P14: attribution.undeclared 'never', 'always', 'solo' and 'sometimes' (unknown, so solo).
- P15: taskSizing {warnSteps 3, maxSteps 6, warnDistinctFiles 2, maxDistinctFiles 4}.
- P16: taskSizing {warnSteps 9, maxSteps 2}. The max is lifted to the warn value: 9/9 steps, file defaults.
- P17: wire types the daemon reads strictly: autoCommit "false" (a string), checkpointCommits 0, commitHooks "true" (a string). Expect On, On and Skipped, because the getCommitScope.ts policy block reads `!== false` and `=== true`.
- P18: taskSizing {warnSteps "9", maxSteps 7.5, warnDistinctFiles 0, maxDistinctFiles -1}. Expect all defaults ('Warn past 8 steps / 5 files, reject past 12 / 10'), because positiveInt in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planSize.ts accepts only integer numbers above 0.
- P19: qualityGate 42 and consolidationBranch true. Expect the disabled quality gate and the default shared landing-branch row, because the wrapper (scripts/moe-agent.sh isinstance(v, str)) and complete_task (typeof === 'string') ignore non-strings.

P18 and P19 encode the daemon and wrapper semantics, NOT today's JetBrains output. They are the expected RED rows of step 2, and step 3 fixes JetBrains to match them. Never edit their expect to match JetBrains.

Error handling: keep the file valid JSON. Check it with plain `node -e` (JSON.parse); no npm.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix the two JetBrains divergences in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt. They are display-only: MoeCommandSender.updateSettings sends only approvalMode, speedModeDelayMs, agentCommand and enableAgentTeams, and only MoeSettingsDialog reads these fields.

(a) Add a private JsonObject.getStrictStringOrDefault(key, default) that honours only a JSON string primitive. Use it for consolidationBranch and qualityGate in parseProjectSettings, keeping .trim().
(b) Add a private JsonObject.getPositiveIntOrNull(key) that honours only a JSON number primitive whose value is an exact Int above 0. Use asBigDecimal.intValueExact() inside try/catch, so 7.5, "9", 0, -1 and out-of-range values all give null. Use it for the four thresholds in parseTaskSizing, keeping the defaults and the maxOf lift.

Leave getIntOrNull and getStringOrDefault unchanged, because other callers use them. KDoc each new helper with the semantics it mirrors: scripts/moe-agent.sh isinstance(v, str) and completeTask.ts typeof === 'string' for (a); planSize.ts positiveInt for (b).

Error handling: neither helper may throw. project.json is hand-editable, and a malformed settings block must degrade to defaults, never blank the board (the existing contract above parseProjectSettings). MoeJsonTest.kt stays unchanged: its malformed-settings rows (0, -4, 9/2) keep passing.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A client-neutral corpus pins what JetBrains' settings dialog shows as the effective landing policy for a given project.settings wire block, defaults included, so that VS Code (VSC-10) can replay it unchanged. JetBrains' parse of taskSizing, qualityGate and consolidationBranch follows the daemon and wrapper semantics: integer numbers above 0 only, and strings only.
acceptanceCriteria: client-settings-policy.json has version 1 and rows P01 to P19, covering every case in the description plus three wire-type rows.
SettingsPolicyCorpusTest checks well-formedness and replays every row through MoeJson.parseState (or null) and effectivePolicyRows, reporting all failing ids at once.
Before the MoeJson fix only P18 and P19 fail; after it every row passes. The Commit board state mutant fails the test.
The full JetBrains suite passes in a snapshot under the jetbrains-gradle lease.
invariants: MoeSettingsDialog.kt, MoeJsonTest.kt and MoeSettingsDialogTest.kt are unchanged.
getIntOrNull and getStringOrDefault keep their behaviour for every other caller.
No MoeJson reader throws on malformed settings.
compatibility: UPDATE_SETTINGS from JetBrains still sends only approvalMode, speedModeDelayMs, agentCommand and enableAgentTeams, so stricter parsing cannot overwrite stored values.
sourceAssumptions: MoeSettingsDialog.kt companion effectivePolicyRows(settings: ProjectSettings?) returns 10 PolicyRow(label, value, detail) entries; PolicyRow is nested in MoeSettingsDialog.
MoeJson.parseState(payload).project.settings is built by the private parseProjectSettings; parseTaskSizing uses getIntOrNull (Gson asInt).
packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planSize.ts positiveInt: typeof number, Number.isInteger and above 0, else the default; a max is lifted to its warn value.
The scripts/moe-agent.sh settings reader treats non-str qualityGate and consolidationBranch as '', and completeTask.ts uses typeof === 'string'.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Corpus rows with WIRE types (P17 to P19) were added beyond the description's list, because they are where two independent clients diverge. Code reading at 9ea87aa6 shows JetBrains already diverges from the daemon in two places:
(1) taskSizing goes through Gson asInt, which parses "9" and truncates 7.5 to 7, while planSize.ts positiveInt rejects both.
(2) consolidationBranch and qualityGate go through getStringOrDefault, which turns 42 or true into a string, while the wrapper and complete_task treat non-strings as unset.
The description pre-authorizes fixing such bugs here, in MoeSettingsDialog.kt or MoeJson.kt. The fix is local to two new strict readers; changing getIntOrNull or getStringOrDefault globally was rejected because they have other callers. P18 and P19 each combine two aspects, so a partial fix still fails the row.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- parseProjectSettings is private. parseState always yields a non-null ProjectSettings (defaults for a missing or null block), so a null corpus row must call effectivePolicyRows(null) directly.
- JetBrains has no SETTINGS_UPDATED handler.
- effectivePolicyRows strings are plain Kotlin, not MoeBundle keys, so the corpus carries the English text itself.
